metaDescription: Six compact electric griddles for one to three people, compared by plate size, wattage, temperature range, storage footprint and everyday cleanup.
introParagraphs: A small electric griddle is a quiet upgrade for anyone who cooks for one or two. It heats a flat plate evenly, so eggs, a grilled cheese or a few pancakes come out without pulling out a full skillet or heating a stove burner.

Small does not mean identical, though. Plates range from 10.5 by 8.5 inches up to 16 by 10, wattage sits at 1200W for most, and the real differences are in temperature range, ledge design and how neatly the unit stores. We evaluated six compact models based on product specs and buyer feedback.

The lineup runs from a personal-size 10-inch unit to mid-size 16-inch plates that still take less room than a family griddle. Each pick suits a different amount of counter, storage and cooking. Read the household and storage sections below to narrow the field quickly, then check the cleaning notes for the coating you prefer.

products.name: Elite Gourmet EGR-2722B Griddle
products.description:
The Elite Gourmet EGR-2722B has the smallest plate in this group at 10.5 by 8.5 inches, yet it still has a 1200W element and a thermostat that climbs to 425F. That combination heats a compact surface in a few minutes. The cool-touch design keeps the body easier to handle.

It works best for one or two people making eggs, sandwiches, a couple of pancakes or quesadillas. The limit is plain: batches are small, and a family-size breakfast will take several rounds. The listing mentions no ledge, tray or drain feature, so grease handling is manual.

The upside is storage. It slides into a drawer or a low shelf that a 16-inch plate never would. Compared with the Presto 07047 at 10.5 by 16 inches, it covers about half the cooking area, and against the 10-inch I-Keukenn it adds a slightly longer plate and the cool-touch body. It is the simplest pick for tight kitchens.

products.name: Presto 07047 16-Inch Griddle
products.description:
The Presto 07047 has a 10.5 by 16 inch cooking area, making it the middle step between a personal griddle and a family-size one. A built-in backstop ledge stops food from sliding off the back edge, and the cool-touch base keeps the front and sides safer to handle. The surface is a PFAS-free ceramic nonstick.

That plate fits most breakfasts for a pair or a small family. Pancakes, French toast and bacon all have room without a crowd. It does not tilt, so grease stays on the surface unless you wipe it away.

Ceramic coatings are happiest with nylon or wooden tools, so metal spatulas should stay in the drawer. It needs more storage space than a compact unit, which is the main downside. At 16 inches it offers a much larger plate than the Elite Gourmet, and it matches the OVENTE's 16 by 10 inches with a more refined ledge and base.

products.name: Chefman Compact Electric Griddle
products.description:
The Chefman Compact keeps a 9.8 by 15.7 inch surface and a removable temperature control. Because the control comes off, the flat top is described as immersible, which simplifies cleanup. A drip tray collects excess oil and grease.

The 200 to 420F range covers the span from keeping food warm to searing a burger. That makes it flexible for breakfast, sandwiches and quick dinners. The probe has to stay dry, so you remove it before washing and reinsert it only when everything is dry.

Its plate is close to the Presto 07047 in size but slightly narrower. Unlike the Presto it has a drip tray, though it lacks the ledge. The extra step of attaching the control each time is the one small chore. Compared with the 10-inch I-Keukenn it holds more food, while still fitting a standard cabinet.

products.name: I-Keukenn 10-Inch Mini Griddle
products.description:
The I-Keukenn is a personal-size griddle with a 10-inch plate and 1200W of heat. The listing describes a textured ceramic skillet coating that is PFAS-free. An adjustable thermostat covers 200 to 425F, which is broad for such a small unit.

It shines in small spaces such as dorm rooms, RV kitchens or studio apartments, because it takes up minimal room in cabinets or drawers. One person can cook an egg and toast on it, or fry a couple of pancakes. The trade-off is capacity, since a 10-inch plate does not suit anyone cooking for a crowd.

Cleanup is easy on the textured ceramic if you use gentle tools. Compared with the Elite Gourmet, it is round-ish and a bit more compact, though the Elite Gourmet adds a cool-touch design. Against the NutriChef at 12 inches it is smaller but has a wider thermostat range, topping out at 425F.

products.name: OVENTE GD1610B 16 x 10 Griddle
products.description:
The OVENTE GD1610B offers a 16 by 10 inch nonstick plate, which gives it more room than most small models. It runs at 1200W with five temperature settings between 200 and 400F, and the listing calls the heating element rapid. The nonstick surface handles pancakes, eggs, bacon and sandwiches.

Five fixed settings are simpler than a continuous dial, although they offer less fine control. That suits cooks who want to pick a number and go. The 400F ceiling is a bit lower than the 425F on the Elite Gourmet and I-Keukenn.

It makes sense for small families or couples who occasionally host. At 16 by 10 inches it is the same size as the Presto 07047 but without the ceramic coating or cool-touch base details. Storage needs are moderate. If you want the largest plate in a budget-friendly small category, this is the one to look at.

products.name: NutriChef 12-Inch Griddle and Crepe Maker
products.description:
The NutriChef is a 12-inch round griddle that doubles as a crepe maker. The circular plate is the right shape for spreading thin batter, so crepes and blintzes come out evenly. It also handles pancakes, eggs and other breakfast items, with adjustable temperature control.

The listing calls it small enough to simplify storage and travel, and it is safe for any countertop or tabletop. That makes it a sensible pick for dorms, camping trips or small tables where you cook at the seat. The drawback is that a round 12-inch plate has less usable area than a 10 by 16 rectangle.

Because the plate is round, long items such as bacon strips do not lay out as neatly as on the OVENTE or Presto 07047. Against the I-Keukenn at 10 inches it adds some cooking diameter. It is the specialist pick of this group, and it is best if crepes are part of your routine.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A small griddle only helps if it fits where you cook and where you store it. The Elite Gourmet is 10.5 by 8.5 inches, while the OVENTE and Presto 07047 reach 16 inches. Measure your drawer or shelf first, then choose the largest plate that still fits comfortably. A mini plate stored easily gets used far more than a large one left in a closet.

Small plates heat quickly, but they still need enough power to recover after loading cold food. The I-Keukenn, Elite Gourmet and OVENTE each list 1200W, which is plenty for a plate under 16 inches. Look for a thermostat rather than a fixed heat so you can lower the setting for eggs. Always preheat before the first pour.

A wider range gives you more recipes. The Chefman covers 200 to 420F, the I-Keukenn 200 to 425F, and the OVENTE 200 to 400F in five steps. Searing burgers wants the upper end, while pancakes and eggs sit in the middle. Continuous dials offer finer control, but fixed settings are quicker to use.

On a small plate, a backstop ledge keeps food on the surface. The Presto 07047 includes one, and the Chefman adds a drip tray for excess oil. Elite Gourmet lists neither, so you wipe fat with a paper towel. If you cook bacon often, favor a ledge or tray, because a drip-free plate is a messier counter.

Most small griddles use a nonstick or ceramic surface that scratches easily. The Presto 07047 and I-Keukenn list PFAS-free ceramic coatings, which need nylon or wooden tools. Let the plate cool fully before washing to avoid warping. Never use metal scrapers, and plan to replace worn plates rather than push through chipping.

Easy cleanup is a major reason to buy a griddle at all. The Chefman has a removable control and an immersible body, so you can rinse the whole plate. Others need a damp cloth and a gentle wipe. The control probe must stay dry in every case, and a drip tray emptied after each use prevents buildup.

howWeEvaluated.title: Plate size and shape
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared plate dimensions from each listing, from the Elite Gourmet at 10.5 by 8.5 inches to the OVENTE and Presto 07047 at 16 inches. Shape counted too, since the NutriChef is round for crepes while the others are rectangles. We scored how many typical breakfast items a plate holds.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and temperature control
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at wattage and range. The I-Keukenn, Elite Gourmet and OVENTE sit at 1200W, and top temperatures run from 400F on the OVENTE to 425F on the I-Keukenn and Elite Gourmet. Thermostat quality and the clarity of settings earned credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Storage and portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We scored footprint and weight cues from the listings. The Elite Gourmet and I-Keukenn lead on compact storage, the NutriChef on tabletop travel, and the Presto 07047 and OVENTE give up some storage for capacity.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleanup and surface
howWeEvaluated.description: We assessed coatings and cleaning features, including the Chefman's removable control, the Presto 07047's PFAS-free ceramic and ledge, and the I-Keukenn's textured skillet surface. Models without a tray or ledge scored lower on mess control.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The Elite Gourmet leads on smallest footprint, the Presto 07047 on mid-size design, and the Chefman on removable-control cleaning. The OVENTE offers the largest 1200W plate and the NutriChef is the crepe specialist. This keeps the ranking tied to use case rather than a single score.

faq.q: What size griddle is enough for one or two people?
faq.a: A plate around 10 by 8 to 12 inches is enough for one or two people. The Elite Gourmet at 10.5 by 8.5 inches and the I-Keukenn at 10 inches cover eggs, toast and a pair of pancakes. If you cook for a third person, step up to the Chefman or Presto 07047.

faq.q: Is 1200 watts enough for a small griddle?
faq.a: Yes. Most compact models, including the Elite Gourmet, I-Keukenn and OVENTE, list 1200W, and that is enough to heat a plate under 16 inches. Always preheat before adding food. You will wait longer for recovery on a 16 inch plate than a 10 inch one.

faq.q: Can I use metal utensils on a small griddle?
faq.a: Usually not. Ceramic and nonstick coatings, as on the Presto 07047 and I-Keukenn, scratch under metal. Use nylon, silicone or wood tools instead. Let the plate cool before washing, and never use abrasive pads.

faq.q: Which small griddle is easiest to clean?
faq.a: The Chefman Compact is the easiest on paper because its control is removable, making the flat top immersible. The probe must stay dry, so remove it before washing. Other models need a damp cloth, and the drip tray should be emptied each time.

faq.q: Is a small griddle better than a skillet?
faq.a: A griddle gives you a flat, evenly heated plate with a thermostat, so you do not need a stove burner. It suits pancakes and sandwiches especially well. A skillet is better for sauces and deep sides, so many people keep both.

faq.q: Do small griddles use a lot of electricity?
faq.a: A 1200W griddle draws about as much as a hair dryer on a medium setting, and it only runs at full power while heating. Once the plate reaches the set temperature, the thermostat cycles the element on and off. Shorter preheats and a lid or foil tent over the food cut the time you spend plugged in. The OVENTE, Elite Gourmet and I-Keukenn all sit at 1200W, so there is little difference between them on this point.

faq.q: Why does a ledge matter on a compact plate?
faq.a: A ledge stops food from sliding off the back, which matters on a plate this small. The Presto 07047 includes a backstop ledge, and the Chefman adds a drip tray for oil. Without either, as on the Elite Gourmet, you steer food with a spatula and wipe grease manually.
